title: A Static for the Terminal
premise: Petra Okonkwo, a xenolinguist whose mind has been reshaped by alien grammar until he no longer dreams in human languages, is the sole archivist of Meridian Station, a dying colony Earth quietly abandoned. When a distress signal arrives in Vessic — a language extinct for two centuries and spoken by no living being — Petra decodes it as a warning: two rival fleets are converging on Meridian's ruins, each believing the other fired first. To keep them apart long enough to evacuate the colonists, Petra fabricates a third fleet from looped transmissions, a lie that grows heavier with every broadcast. In the end, the lie collapses; Petra confesses in both human tongues and Vessic, and his honesty — not his deception — convinces the fleets to stand down, though he loses the station, his archive, and any chance of returning home.
about_author: Sable Delacroix is the pen name of a former radio operator who spent six years on remote relay stations before turning to fiction. Their work explores language as both bridge and battlefield, and they write exclusively at night, claiming the static helps them think.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Petra Okonkwo records his 4,000th archival entry on Meridian Station, noting that he now dreams in the cadence of a dead alien tongue rather than English or Yoruba. His assistant, Wren, begs him to petition Earth for evacuation funds. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Mouth
chapters.summary: A distress burst arrives encoded in Vessic, a language extinct since the Fleet Wars. Petra decodes fragments suggesting an attack that hasn't happened yet. He reports it; Earth's response is automated silence. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: electric dread — the first proof anyone remembers this place exists.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Grave
chapters.summary: Wren intercepts military chatter: the Concord fleet and the Freehold armada are both inbound, each blaming the other for the signal. Petra realizes the transmission was forged — but by whom? POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dawning horror as the colony becomes a pretext for war.

chapters.title: Grammar of a Lie
chapters.summary: Petra proposes the impossible: synthesize a 'third fleet' using Meridian's ancient transmitter array, speaking in Vessic so neither side can verify it. Wren calls it madness; the colonists' council narrowly approves. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: intoxicating power — he can shape reality with syntax alone.

chapters.title: Static Between Worlds
chapters.summary: The false fleet broadcasts its first warning. The Concord vanguard hesitates at the system's edge. But the forgery requires Petra to speak Vessic aloud for hours daily, and the language begins rewriting his waking thoughts too. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: vertigo — fluency becoming possession.

chapters.title: What the Colonists Buried
chapters.summary: Excavating the transmitter's power core, Wren discovers Meridian's founders were Vessic survivors who faked their own extinction — and left a message: 'Do not speak us back.' The lie Petra built may be resurrecting something worse than war. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: betrayal by one's own history.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: Earth sends its final transmission: a termination loop announcing Meridian's official erasure from all registries. The colonists riot; the council demands Petra use the false fleet to seize a ship. He refuses, fracturing the colony. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: love against duty — he protects the truth over the people demanding comfort.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Both fleets enter orbit simultaneously. The forged fleet's pattern is detected as synthetic; Concord and Freehold commanders each assume the other built it. Weapons arm. Petra has hours to decide between confession and escalation. POV: alternating Petra and Wren. Emotional beat: suffocating inevitability.

chapters.title: Confession in Two Tongues
chapters.summary: Petra broadcasts unencrypted, admitting the forgery in English, Yoruba, and fluent Vessic — revealing the founders' survival and begging both fleets to see Meridian as witness, not weapon. The Vessic resonance triggers something in both fleets' old archives: shared grief, older than their feud. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: cathartic surrender of control.

chapters.title: A Static for the Terminal
chapters.summary: The fleets stand down and jointly evacuate the colonists, but the station and Petra's life's archive burn in the atmosphere during departure. Wren survives; Petra chooses to remain until the final entry finishes transmitting. His last recording plays across both fleets' channels. POV: Wren, then Petra's recorded voice. Emotional beat: mournful peace — a voice outlasting its body.
